channel.title: Acme: Light News
channel.description: Positive, lighthearted and unusual current news.

item.title: French archivists rescue family memories one home movie at a time
item.description: A traveling French archive project digitized 22 hours of 8mm and Super 8 home movies during a stop in Antibes, returning forgotten weddings, vacations and childhood scenes to families. The reels also yielded unexpected history, including rare footage of Brigitte Bardot at a local event.

item.title: Coyotes test California's giant wildlife crossing before opening day
item.description: Coyotes have already crossed the 1,250-foot Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing over U.S. 101 near Los Angeles, weeks before its December 2 public opening. Inspired by mountain lion P-22, the landscaped bridge is designed to reconnect habitat split by one of the nation’s busiest freeways.

item.title: Seventy-five sea turtles hatch from the first nests recorded on the U.S. West Coast
item.description: The Aquarium of the Pacific released 75 olive ridley hatchlings from two unprecedented Southern California nests after a 58-day incubation. Experts had never documented sea turtles nesting on the U.S. West Coast, making the tiny swimmers both a scientific first and a hopeful conservation story.

item.title: Romanian prison festival gives 59 inmates a public stage
item.description: Fifty-nine inmates from seven prisons performed at Bucharest’s Nottara Theatre in the 15th Dana Cenusa festival. The program pairs prisoners with theater professionals and uses applause, collaboration and roles ranging from Beckett to original monologues to build confidence and prepare participants for life after custody.

item.title: Italy’s hedgehog hospital names every tiny patient as an act of hope
item.description: At La Ninna rescue center in Piedmont, underweight hoglets receive incubators, fluids, oxygen and individual names before a hoped-for spring release. The donation-funded clinic was caring for about 300 hedgehogs by mid-November, many born too late to reach the weight needed for winter hibernation.

item.title: Ancient Rome’s long-buried Ulpia Library welcomes visitors again
item.description: The restored western building of Trajan’s Ulpia Library is opening to the public after being inaccessible for nearly a century. Visitors can see surviving marble, column fragments and projections explaining a repository that once held Greek scrolls and public records; its Latin-language twin remains beneath a church.

item.title: FDA approves first treatment shown to extend lives in severe childhood disease
item.description: The FDA approved Lembaz, the first treatment shown to help people with infantile-onset Niemann-Pick disease type C live longer. The rare disorder causes cholesterol and other lipids to accumulate in cells; the approval follows two decades of foundational work by National Institutes of Health researchers.

item.title: Cincinnati Zoo gives Fiona a gentle shake to help pass a swallowed hat
item.description: Fiona the hippo is getting unconventional help after swallowing a visitor’s hat: Cincinnati Zoo veterinarians tried a vibration plate to encourage the obstruction to move. An ultrasound showed her intestines still working to pass it, and the zoo continues to monitor its famously resilient star.

item.title: El Dorado turns unwanted aviation fame into a pronunciation lesson
item.description: After a communications failure near El Dorado, Arkansas, was blamed for a nationwide flight disruption, the city used its sudden notoriety to clear up something locals hear constantly: the name is pronounced “El Duh Ray Duh.” Officials are redirecting attention toward the town’s people, history and attractions.

item.title: Pope forgives the pilgrim whose thrown rosary hit him in the eye
item.description: Pope Leo XIV laughed off the rosary that struck his eye during a popemobile ride before a Lima Mass attended by about 1.5 million people. He said the throw reflected profound faith, joked that Peru was something he carried in his heart and eye, and forgave the enthusiastic pilgrim.

item.title: Baby oysters return to a Scottish firth after more than a century
item.description: Native oysters are reproducing in the Dornoch Firth for the first time since the population was fished out in the late 1800s. Scientists and volunteers have restored more than 140,000 juveniles since 2017; the newly found babies show that the reef can now begin rebuilding itself.

item.title: Healthy corals can nurse bleached neighbors back to health
item.description: Researchers found that a healthy coral touching a bleached one can fuse with it and form a bridge carrying nutrients and symbiotic algae. The damaged coral continued recovering after the helper was removed, suggesting a surprisingly simple path toward future reef restoration.

item.title: Buffett donates another $5.5 billion to family foundations
item.description: Warren Buffett converted 1,800 Berkshire Hathaway Class A shares and donated the resulting stock, worth roughly $5.5 billion, to four family foundations. His Thanksgiving letter again urged readers to practice kindness, arguing that goodness grows when it is shared.

item.title: Millions of red crabs begin Christmas Island migration
item.description: Christmas Island’s annual red-crab migration is underway, sending millions of bright crustaceans from the forest toward the sea. The national park has opened bridges and road crossings for the travelers and is carrying live video of the spectacle for viewers far from the Indian Ocean.

item.title: Volunteer drives 1,400 kilometres to save stranded turtle
item.description: Wildlife carer Letesha Heslewood made a 16-hour round trip across Western Australia to collect a stranded loggerhead turtle nicknamed Shaggy. The exhausted animal is now eating squid and recovering in a heated tank at Bunbury’s Dolphin Discovery Centre.
